simple.meaning: לַח (lach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “fresh , i.e. unused or undried.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Genesis, Numbers, Judges, Ezekiel, beginning at Genesis 30:37. Its contexts include family line, righteousness, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לַח (H3892).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: לַח (lach) / H3892 is traced through Genesis 30:37, Numbers 6:3, Judges 16:7, Judges 16:8 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H3892. lach לַח adjective moist, fresh, new ; — ׳ל Gen 30:37 ; Ezek 21:3 ; לָ֑ח 17:24 ; plural לַחִים Num 6:3 2 t.; — 1 moist, fresh , of trees, fruit, etc.; לַח לִבְנֶה Gen 30:37 (J); ל ׳עֵץ Ezek 17:24 ; 21:3 ; grapes ל ׳עֲנָבִים Num 6:3 . 2 new , of cords, ל ׳יְתָרִים Judg 16:7-8 , probably made of fresh sinews of animal (compare Syriac PS 1652 ; GFM on the passage )
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to be new;
